## What you do not need {#what-you-do-not-need-today}

::: {.none}
- No git, no GitHub account and no OSF account – we read the OSF from the outside, as any reader can
- Nothing more to install: the workspace that you installed before the day holds every task, and you work in it, in your IDE
- This deck runs R inside the browser and shows each step with its output, so it carries the work if your installation fails
- Nothing leaves your machine except what you choose to send
:::

::: {.fragment}
**Do this now:** open the workspace folder in your IDE. If your installation failed, open this deck in a tab of your own instead, and leave it to load.
:::

::: notes
Before anything else, a word on what you do not need today. You do not need git, a GitHub account or an OSF account, because we read the OSF from the outside, as any reader can. You do not need to install anything more either: you installed the workspace before the day, and that is where you work, because every task of the day is in its report. This deck is what I drive on the shared screen. R runs inside it, in the browser, so on each hands-on slide I run the step in front of you, and you can compare my output with yours. If your installation has failed, open the deck in a tab of your own and work in its cells; the browser lab on the course site holds the same tasks as a page. One thing to do right now, while I talk: open the workspace folder in your IDE.
:::
